questions.title: Section A: Multiple Choice, Matching, Terminology and True/False

subQuestions.questionText: The following is NOT a part of a pig stomach:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B - Reticulum (2 marks)
The reticulum is one of the four compartments of a ruminant stomach. A pig has a simple (monogastric) stomach made up of the cardia, fundus, body and pylorus.

subQuestions.questionText: The structure of the alimentary canal of a young ruminant differs from that of an adult ruminant because in the young ruminant ...
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D - only oesophageal groove and abomasum are functional (2 marks)
In a young (unweaned) ruminant the rumen, reticulum and omasum are undeveloped. Milk bypasses the rumen via the oesophageal groove and is digested in the abomasum (the only functional stomach compartment).

options.A: the rumen and abomasum are well developed.
options.B: the omasum is fully developed and the abomasum is underdeveloped.
options.C: only the rumen and reticulum are functional.
options.D: only oesophageal groove and abomasum are functional.

subQuestions.questionText: The mineral elements that are needed by farm animals in large quantities:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C - Calcium, magnesium and sulphur (2 marks)
Calcium, magnesium and sulphur are macro-minerals, required in large amounts. Iron, cobalt, copper, selenium and zinc are trace (micro) minerals needed only in small amounts.

subQuestions.questionText:
The statements below refer to essential amino acids:
(i) They cannot be synthesized by non-ruminants.
(ii) They are found in the protein of animal origin.
(iii) Both plant and animal protein contain essential amino acids.
(iv) They can be provided to animals through the feed.
Choose the CORRECT combination:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A - (i), (ii) and (iv) (2 marks)
Essential amino acids cannot be synthesised by non-ruminants, occur in animal protein and must be supplied in the feed. Statement (iii) is incorrect because not all plant proteins contain all the essential amino acids.

subQuestions.questionText: The rapid spread of infectious diseases over a very large area:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B - Pandemic (2 marks)
A pandemic is the rapid spread of an infectious disease over a very large area (across countries/continents). Endemic = constantly present in an area; sporadic = occurring irregularly; acute = short and severe course.

subQuestions.questionText:
Subsistence livestock farmers who cannot afford expensive modern technologies may use the following methods to control parasites:
(i) Burning the veld
(ii) Herbal remedies
(iii) Rotational grazing
(iv) Electric spray race
Choose the CORRECT combination:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A - (i), (ii) and (iii) (2 marks)
Burning the veld, herbal remedies and rotational grazing are low-cost methods available to subsistence farmers. An electric spray race (iv) is an expensive modern technology.

subQuestions.questionText: The following is a disadvantage of keeping pigs in a free-range system:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C - May take more time for pigs to reach the marketing stage (2 marks)
In a free-range system pigs use energy moving around and growth is slower, so they take longer to reach market weight. The other options are advantages of free-range systems.

options.A: Lower feed costs on good pastures
options.C: May take more time for pigs to reach the marketing stage

subQuestions.questionText: The diagram in the question paper shows an animal (an ox) with four labelled areas relating to how close a handler can move to it: Area A is a narrow wedge just behind and to the side of the animal's hindquarters; Area B is a wide forward zone in front of the animal marked with 45° and 90° angles; Area C is the large outer circle surrounding the whole animal; Area D points to the animal's shoulder/body. The area in the diagram that represents the distance within which a person can approach an animal before it moves away is ...
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C - Area C (2 marks)
Area C, the outer circle around the animal, is the flight zone – the boundary within which the approach of a person causes the animal to move away.

subQuestions.questionText: The scrotum regulates the temperature during spermatogenesis by …
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A - contracting when conditions are cold and relaxing when conditions are hot (2 marks)
In cold conditions the scrotal muscles (dartos/cremaster) contract to pull the testes closer to the body for warmth; in hot conditions they relax to lower the testes away from the body to cool them, keeping the testes a few degrees below body temperature for normal sperm production.

options.A: contracting when conditions are cold and relaxing when conditions are hot.
options.B: pulling the testes up when conditions are hot.
options.C: relaxing the testes when temperatures are low.

subQuestions.questionText: A condition where the foetus dies after the hard skeleton and skin have been formed without abortion and secondary infection:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C - Mummification (2 marks)
Mummification is when a dead foetus (already having a hard skeleton and skin) is retained in the uterus and dries out, with no abortion and no secondary infection. Maceration involves decomposition/infection; dropsy is fluid accumulation; prolapse is displacement of an organ.

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether each of the descriptions in COLUMN B applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B or NONE of the items in COLUMN A. Write A only, B only, both A and B or none.
COLUMN A: A: Bile; B: Hydrochloric acid
COLUMN B: Counteracts putrefaction in the stomach of an animal
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: B only (2 marks)
Hydrochloric acid in the stomach creates an acidic environment that kills bacteria and counteracts putrefaction (decay) of food. Bile is released into the small intestine and emulsifies fat.

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether each of the descriptions in COLUMN B applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B or NONE of the items in COLUMN A.
COLUMN A: A: Dry rolling; B: Dry heating
COLUMN B: Method to increase digestibility of grains
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Both A and B (2 marks)
Both dry rolling (mechanically cracking the grain) and dry heating (roasting) are physical processing methods used to increase the digestibility of grains.

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether each of the descriptions in COLUMN B applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B or NONE of the items in COLUMN A.
COLUMN A: A: Pulse rate; B: Respiratory rate
COLUMN B: The number of heartbeats in one minute
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: A only (2 marks)
Pulse rate is the number of heartbeats per minute. Respiratory rate is the number of breaths per minute.

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether each of the descriptions in COLUMN B applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B or NONE of the items in COLUMN A.
COLUMN A: A: Deep litter; B: Free range
COLUMN B: The system whereby chickens are kept in small wire cages while laying eggs for their entire lives
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: None (2 marks)
Keeping layers in small wire cages for their entire productive lives is the battery cage system. In the deep litter system birds move freely on a litter-covered floor; in free range they have access to an outdoor run.

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether each of the descriptions in COLUMN B applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B or NONE of the items in COLUMN A.
COLUMN A: A: Perimetrium; B: Endometrium
COLUMN B: Embryonic membrane surrounding the foetus
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: None (2 marks)
The perimetrium and endometrium are layers of the uterine wall (outer serous layer and inner lining respectively). The embryonic membranes surrounding the foetus are the amnion, chorion and allantois.

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description. Write only the word/term.
The total amount of energy released as heat when a feed is completely burnt down.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Gross energy / GE (2 marks)
Gross energy is the total heat energy released when a feed is completely combusted (burnt) in a bomb calorimeter.

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description. Write only the word/term.
An organism that carries a disease-causing agent.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Vector (2 marks)
A vector is an organism (e.g. a tick or mosquito) that carries and transmits a disease-causing pathogen from one host to another.

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description. Write only the word/term.
The failure of a cow to expel the placenta within 12–24 hours after parturition.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Placenta retention / retained placenta (2 marks)
Retained placenta (retentio secundinarum) is the failure of a cow to expel the foetal membranes within about 12–24 hours after calving.

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description. Write only the word/term.
The process by which the male reproductive cells are formed.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Spermatogenesis (2 marks)
Spermatogenesis is the process of formation and development of sperm cells (male gametes) in the seminiferous tubules of the testis.

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description. Write only the word/term.
A device placed around the lower leg of a cow to detect her movement and increased activities during oestrus.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Pedometer (2 marks)
A pedometer is fitted to a cow's leg to measure the number of steps/activity; a marked increase in activity indicates that the cow is on heat (oestrus).

subQuestions.questionText:
Change the UNDERLINED WORD(S) in the following statement to make it TRUE. Write only the answer.
Deformation and ulceration of the cornea of an eye resulting in impaired vision in farm animals is due to a deficiency of vitamin D.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Vitamin A / retinol (1 mark)
Vitamin A deficiency causes deformation and ulceration of the cornea (xerophthalmia) and night blindness. Vitamin D deficiency causes rickets/osteomalacia.

subQuestions.questionText:
Change the UNDERLINED WORD(S) in the following statement to make it TRUE. Write only the answer.
A halter is a fixed handling facility attached to the end of a crush used to restrain cattle by the head.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Neck clamp / head clamp / head gate (1 mark)
A neck clamp (head gate) is the fixed head-restraining device at the front end of a crush. A halter is a rope/strap head collar, not a fixed facility.

subQuestions.questionText:
Change the UNDERLINED WORD(S) in the following statement to make it TRUE. Write only the answer.
The sperm duct is a common excretory and reproductive canal in male animals.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Urethra (1 mark)
The urethra is the common passage for both urine (excretory) and semen (reproductive) in the male. The sperm duct (vas deferens) only carries sperm.

subQuestions.questionText:
Change the UNDERLINED WORD(S) in the following statement to make it TRUE. Write only the answer.
Pregnancy is the period that lasts for approximately 305 days in which a dairy cow produces milk.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Lactation (1 mark)
Lactation is the period (about 305 days in a standard dairy record) during which a cow produces milk after calving. Pregnancy (gestation) in a cow lasts about 283 days.

subQuestions.questionText:
Change the UNDERLINED WORD(S) in the following statement to make it TRUE. Write only the answer.
Hypoplasia is a condition where a male animal shows interest in a female, but lacks the ability to serve the female animals.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Impotence (1 mark)
Impotence is the inability of a male to mate/serve the female even though it shows sexual interest (libido). Hypoplasia is the underdevelopment of the testes.

subQuestions.questionText:
The table below indicates the intake and flow of food in two farm animals.
COLUMN A: Animal ingests food using the lips and tongue; the teeth grind the food; chemical digestion starts in the mouth through amylase; food is pushed down the oesophagus into the stomach where it is digested further by enzymes.
COLUMN B: Animal ingests food through pecking; food moves into the oesophagus where it is moistened, softened and stored; both physical and chemical digestion occur in the stomach.
Name the farm animal referred to in:
(a) COLUMN A
(b) COLUMN B
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) COLUMN A - Pig (1 mark)
(b) COLUMN B - Fowl / chicken / poultry (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Identify, in the table above, a reason for the answers to QUESTION 2.1.1(a) and 2.1.1(b) above.
subQuestions.memoText:
COLUMN A (pig) – any ONE (1 mark):
• Chemical digestion starts from the mouth through amylase
• Ingests food using the lips and tongue
• The teeth grind the food
• Food is pushed down the oesophagus into the stomach where it is digested further by enzymes

COLUMN B (fowl) – any ONE (1 mark):
• Animal ingests food by pecking
• Food is moistened, softened and stored (in the crop)
• Physical and chemical digestion occur in the stomach (proventriculus and gizzard)

subQuestions.questionText: Give the structural difference in the large intestines of the farm animals in COLUMN A and COLUMN B respectively.
subQuestions.memoText:
COLUMN A (pig) - There is one caecum / the blind gut (colon) of the pig is long / there is a rectum (1 mark)
COLUMN B (fowl) - There are two caeca / the blind gut (colon) of a chicken is short / there is no rectum (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
The diagram in the question paper shows a section of the alimentary canal in farm animals with the associated organs labelled A to E: A is the large lobed organ (liver); B is the small sac lying under the liver (gall bladder); C is the first part of the small intestine into which the ducts open (duodenum); D is the elongated glandular organ lying in the loop of the duodenum (pancreas); E is the duct running from the liver towards C (hepatic/bile duct).
Write down the letter (A–E) that represents the part where EACH of the following occurs:
(a) Soluble food particles move into the blood stream
(b) Storage of fat-soluble vitamins
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) C (1 mark) – the duodenum/small intestine, where absorption of soluble food into the blood takes place
(b) A (1 mark) – the liver, which stores fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K)

subQuestions.questionText: Name TWO digestive juices that are deposited into part C (the duodenum).
subQuestions.memoText:
• Bile (1 mark)
• Pancreatic juice (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Name the fat-digesting enzyme secreted in part D (the pancreas).
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Lipase (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO reasons for the breaking down of fat by the juice contained in part B (bile in the gall bladder).
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• To increase the surface area (of the fat for enzyme action)
• Allows lipase to work better / to enhance chemical digestion
• To improve the absorption of fatty acids / assists with the absorption of fat-soluble vitamins A, D, E, K

subQuestions.questionText:
Farm animals may chew foreign objects due to certain mineral deficiencies.
Name the mineral that is deficient in the farm animals in the statement above.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Phosphorus / P (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Name the condition where farm animals show the deficiency mentioned in QUESTION 2.3.1.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Pica (depraved appetite) (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give an example of a feed supplement that could be used to address the condition named in QUESTION 2.3.2.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Bone meal / mineral lick (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
The table below shows different animal feeds with the percentages of digestible protein (DP):
A. Maize meal – 9% DP
B. Maize stalk – 4% DP
C. Fish meal – 36% DP
Classify maize meal and maize stalk into main types of feeds.
subQuestions.memoText:
Maize meal - Concentrate (1 mark)
Maize stalk - Roughage (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate the importance of feeding maize stalk to EACH of the following farm animals:
(a) Young ruminant
(b) Adult ruminant
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Young ruminant - Stimulates the development of the rumen / fore stomach (1 mark)
(b) Adult ruminant - any ONE (1 mark):
• Ensures normal functioning of the rumen / prevents bloating
• Stimulates the production of butterfat in milk
• Supplies bulkiness to the ration
• Provides energy for maintenance

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the ratio at which maize meal (9% DP) and fish meal (36% DP) should be mixed to get a feed with 15% DP. Show ALL calculations.
subQuestions.memoText:
Using the Pearson square method with 15% DP in the centre:
• Parts of fish meal = 15 − 9 = 6 parts ✓ (1 mark)
• Parts of maize meal = 36 − 15 = 21 parts ✓ (1 mark)
• Correct use of 15% as the desired value in the centre ✓ (1 mark)
• Ratio: Maize meal : Fish meal = 21 : 6 ✓ OR Fish meal : Maize meal = 6 : 21 ✓ (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
A farm animal consumed 15 kg of hay with a dry matter content of 84% and excreted 3,5 kg dry manure.
Calculate the digestibility co-efficiency of the feed in the statement above. Show ALL calculations.
subQuestions.memoText:
Step 1 – Dry matter intake: DM = 15 kg × 84% (0,84) = 12,6 kg ✓✓ (2 marks)
Step 2 – Formula: DC = [(Dry material intake − Dry mass of manure) ÷ Dry material intake] × 100 ✓ (1 mark)
Step 3 – Substitution: = [(12,6 kg − 3,5 kg) ÷ 12,6 kg] × 100 ✓ (1 mark)
Step 4 – Answer: = 72,2% ✓ (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give the percentage of excreted material.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: 27,8% (1 mark)
(100% − 72,2% digested = 27,8% excreted)

subQuestions.questionText:
The table below shows the fodder flow plan over a period of six months:
Grazing available (kg/ha): Jan 1 400; Feb 1 200; March 950; April 800; May 500; June 100
Supplementary feed requirement (kg/animal/day): Jan 0; Feb 0; March 2; April 3; May 5; June 8
Identify the month in which it will be most advisable to reduce the number of farm animals.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: June (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to the data above to justify the answer in QUESTION 2.6.1.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE (1 mark):
• Feed (grazing) availability is at its lowest (100 kg/ha)
• The most supplementary feed is required (8 kg/animal/day)

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the total feed available (in tons) for the month April if the farmer has 5 hectares available for grazing. Show ALL calculations.
subQuestions.memoText:
Step 1: 800 kg/ha × 5 ha = 4 000 kg ✓ (1 mark)
Step 2: 4 000 kg ÷ 1 000 kg ✓ (1 mark)
Step 3: = 4 tons ✓ (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
The picture in the question paper shows animal behaviour under hot conditions: a group of dairy cattle standing under the shade of trees along a river, with one cow standing in the water.
Identify TWO visible actions that the cattle in the picture above take to reduce the effects of heat.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Standing under trees / in the shade for protection from the sun
• Standing in the water to cool the body
• Standing apart / away from each other

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate TWO reasons why shelter is important to farm animals.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Increases the survival rate of young animals
• Protects animals from predators / theft
• Enables the control of diseases and parasites
• Provides an ideal temperature / protects animals against adverse weather conditions
• Prevents dehydration
• Maximises production

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO requirements of the vehicle that transports farm animals.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Floors should not be slippery
• Adequate ventilation
• Rails must be high and strong
• No sharp edges that can harm / hurt the animals
• The vehicle should be clean / hygienic
• Must have enough space

subQuestions.questionText:
The table below shows relative changes in the expected dry matter intake (DMI), milk yield and water intake with increasing environmental temperature:
Temperature 20 °C: DMI 18,2 kg; Milk yield 27 L; Water intake 68 L
Temperature 25 °C: DMI 17,6 kg; Milk yield 25 L; Water intake 74 L
Temperature 30 °C: DMI 16,9 kg; Milk yield 23 L; Water intake 79 L
Temperature 35 °C: DMI 16,7 kg; Milk yield 18 L; Water intake 120 L
Temperature 40 °C: DMI 10,2 kg; Milk yield 12 L; Water intake 106 L
Identify the main farm product produced in the table above.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Milk (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Describe the relationship between dry matter intake, milk yield and water intake when the environmental temperature increases.
subQuestions.memoText:
As the environmental temperature increases:
• Dry matter intake decreases / cows eat less feed ✓ (1 mark)
• Milk yield decreases / less milk is produced ✓ (1 mark)
• Water intake increases / cows drink more water ✓ (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
The graph in the question paper (‘Live weight of animals over a period of time’) shows the average live weight (kg, y-axis, 0–600) of farm animals against age (years, x-axis, 0–2,5) for Farmer A and Farmer B, who use different production systems. Farmer A’s curve rises steeply and steadily, reaching about 550 kg by roughly 1,6 years. Farmer B’s curve rises more slowly, levels off at about 400 kg between roughly 1,5 and 2 years, and then rises again to about 550 kg by roughly 2,3 years.
Identify the farmer that represents EACH of the following:
(a) Extensive production system
(b) Intensive production system
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Extensive production system - Farmer B (1 mark)
(b) Intensive production system - Farmer A (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Justify the answers to QUESTION 3.3.1(a) and 3.3.1(b).
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Extensive (Farmer B) - The herd took longer to reach the live weight of 550 kg / it has a slower growth rate ✓ (1 mark)
(b) Intensive (Farmer A) - The herd took less time to reach the live weight of 550 kg / it has a faster growth rate ✓ (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Identify a disadvantage with regard to the input costs of the intensive production system.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Input costs are high / it is expensive (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
The Department of Agriculture reported several foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) outbreaks in different areas of South Africa. This led to a ban on the export of animals and their products. Veterinarians were then deployed to the affected areas and infected animals were separated from non-infected animals.
Indicate the pathogen that causes the disease in the scenario above.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Virus (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO main symptoms of foot-and-mouth disease in farm animals.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Blister-like lesions (on the mouth, tongue, feet and teats)
• Painful ulcers
• Sticky, foamy salivation
• Severe lameness / unable to walk / limping
• Nasal discharge

subQuestions.questionText: Identify, in the scenario above, TWO roles of the state regarding animal disease control.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Public awareness / reporting the outbreak of FMD
• Quarantine services / separation / isolation of infected animals
• Veterinarian services (deploying vets to affected areas)
• Banning of exports

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO economic impacts of foot-and-mouth disease on South Africa.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• International trade decreases / export bans
• Reduced food security
• Decreased production
• Loss of income / profit / jobs
• High costs to control, prevent and treat the disease
• Death of animals / stock losses

subQuestions.questionText:
The pictures in the question paper (labelled A to D) show different methods used to administer medication to farm animals: A shows animals inside an enclosed spray chamber; B shows a pig restrained on its back being treated by mouth; C shows an animal’s head being held while liquid is given by mouth (drenching); D shows cattle walking/swimming through a long plunge dip tank.
Write down the letters (A–D) that represent TWO methods in the pictures above that can be used for the control of external parasites.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of A, B, D (1 mark each):
• A – spray chamber / spray race (dipping fluid applied to the body surface)
• B – pour-on / topical application
• D – plunge dip

subQuestions.questionText: Write down the letters (A–D) that represent TWO methods in the pictures above that can be used for the treatment of internal parasites.
subQuestions.memoText:
B and C (1 mark each):
• B – oral dosing of a pig
• C – oral drenching (giving a liquid anthelmintic by mouth)

subQuestions.questionText:
The pictures in the question paper (labelled A to D) show different organisms harmful to farm animals: A is a mosquito; B is an engorged tick; C is a mass of long, ribbon-like worms; D is a hard tick (bont tick).
Give a term that describes the organisms in A, B, C and D.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Parasites (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Classify the organisms in B and C.
subQuestions.memoText:
B - External / ecto-parasite (1 mark)
C - Internal / endo-parasite (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Identify the organism (A, B, C or D) that is responsible for transmitting EACH of the following diseases:
(a) Redwater
(b) Rift Valley fever (RVF)
(c) Heartwater
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Redwater - B / blue tick (1 mark)
(b) Rift Valley fever (RVF) - A / mosquito (1 mark)
(c) Heartwater - D / bont tick (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: List THREE plants that are poisonous to farm animals.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any THREE (1 mark each):
• Thorn apple / devil's apple
• Poison bulb / slangkop
• Poison ivy
• Maize fungus
• Lantana camara
• Tulp (tulip)
• Seneciosis (ragwort)
• Gousiektebossie
• Diplodiosis
• Poison leaf / gifblaar
• Geeldikkop
• Gousiekte
• Vermeersiekte

subQuestions.questionText:
The diagram in the question paper shows the reproductive system of a female farm animal, with parts labelled A to E: A is a small oval structure at the end of each horn (ovary); B is the thin, coiled tube leading from the ovary (oviduct / fallopian tube); C is the paired curved horns of the uterus (uterine horn); D is the narrow, thick-walled neck between the uterus and vagina (cervix); E is the wide passage leading to the exterior (vagina).
Write down the letters (A–E) that represent TWO secondary sex organs in the diagram above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of B, C, D, E (1 mark each) – oviduct, uterus, cervix, vagina.
(A, the ovary, is a primary sex organ / gonad.)

subQuestions.questionText:
Write down the letter (A–E) that represents the part where EACH of the following occurs:
(a) Fertilisation
(b) Secretion from these glands provides nutrients for developing embryos
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Fertilisation - B (oviduct / fallopian tube) (1 mark)
(b) Nutrient secretion for developing embryos - C (uterus / endometrial glands) (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
State the function of D (the cervix) under the following conditions:
(a) During mating
(b) During pregnancy
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) During mating - Opens to allow the passage of semen into the uterus (1 mark)
(b) During pregnancy - Closes and seals the uterus with a thick mucus secretion (mucus plug) to prevent microbial infection of the uterus (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
The graph in the question paper shows the hormonal levels of a female farm animal during the reproduction cycle, plotted against the oestrus cycle in days. Progesterone (dashed line) is low at oestrus, rises to a plateau in the middle of the cycle and then falls sharply just before the next oestrus. Oestrogen (solid line) peaks sharply just before each oestrus and then drops to a low level. Two ‘Oestrus’ periods are marked, roughly 21 days apart.
Define the concept oestrus.
subQuestions.memoText: Oestrus is the period when a non-pregnant female animal ✓ is receptive to the male / will allow mating ✓ (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate whether the female farm animal represented in the graph above is pregnant or not.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: The female animal is NOT pregnant (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give a reason, based on the data in the graph, to support the answer to QUESTION 4.2.2.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE (1 mark):
• The animal is showing a normal (repeating) oestrus cycle
• The progesterone level is decreasing (not maintained)
• The oestrogen level is increasing again
• There is a re-appearance of oestrus

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the expected level of FSH of this female farm animal from day 17 to day 20.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: FSH level will be high (1 mark)
(FSH rises towards the end of the cycle to stimulate the development of new Graafian follicles for the next oestrus.)

subQuestions.questionText:
The table below shows the percentage (%) fat, protein and lactose in the milk of dairy cows during certain times:
Week 5: Fat 4,0; Protein 3,0; Lactose 5,0
Week 10: Fat 4,1; Protein 3,2; Lactose 4,9
Week 15: Fat 4,2; Protein 3,5; Lactose 4,8

subQuestions.questionText:
Cattle breeders can increase the number of offspring by artificially bringing all the cows in oestrus at approximately the same time.
Identify the process in the scenario above.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Synchronisation of oestrus (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Name TWO techniques or methods used in the process identified in QUESTION 4.4.1.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Prostaglandin injection
• Synthetic progesterone / oestradiol injection
• Gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) injection
• Vaginal insertion of a progesterone device (CIDR)
• MGA / progestagen mixed with the feed

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO disadvantages of the process identified in QUESTION 4.4.1.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• High management inputs / skills / technology are required
• Adequate facilities are required
• High costs / expensive
• Labour intensive
• Time consuming
• Pregnancy tests must be done frequently

subQuestions.questionText:
Arrange the statements relating to the stages of mating below in sequential order. Write down ONLY the letters (A–E).
A Penetration of the vagina
B Bull jumps off
C Bull shows interest in cows due to increased level of pheromones
D Bull stands on its hind legs with chest on the female animal's rump
E Bull releases sperm cells
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct sequential order (1 mark for each letter in the correct position):
C – D – A – E – B

subQuestions.questionText:
The picture in the question paper shows a cow in the process of giving birth, with the calf’s front legs and head protruding from the vulva.
Name the stage of parturition illustrated in the picture above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE (1 mark):
• Expulsion / ejection of the foetus
• Delivery (of the calf)

subQuestions.questionText: Give the term for a situation when a cow is unable to calve on her own.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Dystocia (difficult birth) (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate TWO calf-related problems that can negatively affect parturition.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Calves with high birth weights / large calves
• Bull calves normally have higher birth weights
• Malformed calves / congenital defects / hydrocephalus
• Multiple births / twins
• Incorrect position of the calf / posterior presentation

subQuestions.questionText:
Diagrams A and B in the question paper show the fusions of male and female gametes and the development of the zygotes. In Diagram A, one sperm cell (n) fuses with one ovum (n) to form a single structure, which then splits into two cells that each develop into an offspring. In Diagram B, two separate sperm cells (n) each fuse with a separate ovum (n) to form two separate 2n zygotes, which each develop into an offspring.
Identify the type of multiple births that resulted from the fusion represented in:
(a) Diagram A
(b) Diagram B
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Diagram A - Identical / monozygotic twins (1 mark)
(b) Diagram B - Fraternal / non-identical / dizygotic twins (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Differentiate between the two multiple births identified in QUESTION 4.7.1.
subQuestions.memoText:
Monozygotic (identical) - Formed from the fertilisation of a single ovum (by one sperm), which then divides (1 mark)
Dizygotic (fraternal) - Formed from the fertilisation of two different ova (by two separate sperm cells) (1 mark)
